explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. `ModularCurve.SharpUnitNecessary` is defined in the library itself, in `Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_EtaQuotient.lean`. It says: if a continuous function H, invariant under Γ₀(ℓ), satisfies H^(ℓ-1) = (Δ(τ)/Δ(ℓ•τ))^m, then `eisensteinNumerator ℓ` divides m. Both `eisensteinNumerator` and `heckeDiagMatrix` (cast here as ℓ•τ) are part of the library's own setup, and Mathlib has no statement of this kind about eta quotients. The current proof just calls the library lemma `DedekindEtaLog.sharpUnitNecessary_of_mod_twelve_eq_five`, which is not in Mathlib, so the proof gives no lead into Mathlib either. All of the theorem's mathematical content lies in the library's own definitions.
